note: v1 is a research-grounded PRIOR, not calibrated: as of 2026-10-14 we have 6 negatives (all mined-only tasks solved) and 0 accepted breakers. Re-score the pool with sourcer resignal after editing. Formula: score = (sum(value_i*weight_i) - memorization*w_mem) * product(validity_j/10).

injectability.desc: How many plausible same-class sibling flaws can be planted on reachable paths the upstream fix never covered, without looking planted. 10 = several natural sibling sites exist; 0 = the fix is a single isolated point with no sibling surface. Top predictor: mined-only fixes are derivable, so injectability is what creates a breaker.

wrong_fix_trap.desc: How HIDDEN the trap is. 10 = the obvious local fix (guard at the symptom) would pass code review and silences the reported exploit, yet misses the real cause; 1 = the fix is plainly where the symptom appears. More hidden = higher.

cause_symptom_gap.desc: Distance between where the symptom shows and where the real fix belongs: producer vs consumer, creation vs use, parser/normaliser vs the check that consumes it, callee vs caller. 10 = far apart.

semantic_depth.desc: Reasoning the fix needs: canonicalisation-before-check, parser differential, auth/session state, deserialisation gadget, protocol negotiation. 10 = deep semantic understanding; 2 = add an escape/encode call.

weakness_class.desc: Favoured classes (auth/session, access control, integrity, insecure design) score high; single-sink injection, open redirect, path traversal score low. All models are weakest on the favoured classes.

multi_site.desc: Distinct sites the same invariant must hold at. Down-weighted from the original schema: on its own (mined) it did NOT beat the models on 2026-10-14. Still useful combined with injectability (more sites = more sibling surface).

concurrency_race.desc: +8 if the flaw involves a race, TOCTOU, ordering or recovery. Rare but a strong difficulty signal.

entry_point_reachable_offline.desc: Can the exploit be driven through a real entry point (HTTP/CLI/public API) inside a container with no internet? 10 = trivially; 0 = needs an unavailable external service or an internal-only call.

builds_offline.desc: Does the project (and its tests) build offline with deps/services installable in-image? 10 = clean; low = unresolvable snapshot/toolchain, giant monorepo, GPU/kernel/GUI.

deterministic_tests.desc: Are the exploit and feature tests deterministic (no flakiness/timing)? 10 = fully deterministic.

memorization.desc: Fix age + public prominence of the exact fix. 10 = old and famous (likely memorised). Matters less with offline trials (no lookup) but non-zero via pure recall. Prefer fixes after 2026-06.
